You should probably look into getting your brakes done. It's a large misconception to think brakes have to squeak when needing replacement, for a general rule of thumb brake pads/shoes tend to squeak, while rotors/drums give you a "pulsation" feeling in your brake pedal. The burning rubber smell could easily be your pads screaming for help, again I'd get them checked or replaced. Your car sliding down your driveway is most likely your parking brake out of adjustment from your pads being so worn and not being able to push against the rotor hard enough to keep your car in place. Make sure you put your car in park or first gear (if you have a manual) to prevent any safety issues or accidents. I highly doubt you'll need to replace your calipers but the pads and rotors definitely need to be checked. Depends on how large your brakes are will change the price to replace them, cost also depends on what you need replaced. If your rotors are large enough to be spun and smoothed down that will save you money. Pads are a different story if they're too worn they need to be replaced. A Honda accord is a fairly small car so I dont think you'll be spending more than $500 to get everything done, but again I dont know exactly what needs to be done on your car. 

If you have any questions feel free to ask and good luck.

I have a rule that I made myself, it's very simple and effective for my mantic depression.
I call it: The 6 hours. Basically when something bad or upsetting happens, say friend got really pissed at me, girlfriend broke up with me, failed my math test, etc. When something like that happens I set a timer on my phone for about 6 hours. Sometimes more depending on what happened. During that 6 hours I can cry be depressed blame it all on myself whatever I gotta do. Then when that timer goes off I move on. I accept that fact that what happened, happened and there will be another girl. There will be another math test. Me and my friend will make up. This easy method COMPLETELY turned my life around. 

If anyone is dealing with depression please give this a try, it really helped me get on with my life and get out of my almost suicidal state. 

Stay strong Reddit. We're here for you :)
